synopsis: The European Commission requests product-law standards from CEN and CENELEC and publishes references that make them harmonized; in 2026 it was still preparing the new Machinery Regulation list, so harmonization of EN 474 and EN ISO 21815 remained unverified [f15077, f2208, f15081]. The corpus leaves classification of frozen, non-learning perception models unresolved, including whether they count as “self-evolving,” pending Commission guidance or delegated acts [f2091, f2369]. The Digital Omnibus was adopted on 8 July 2026 and entered into force on 27 July 2026, with both dates reported in EUR-Lex and the Commission announcement [f10311, f10312]. It moved Annex III high-risk AI obligations to 2 December 2027 and Annex I product-safety-component obligations, including machinery, to 2 August 2028 [f9797, f9798, f10313]. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 empowers the Commission to add machinery AI health-and-safety requirements through delegated acts; secondary summaries say these should apply by 2 August 2028, but their content and timing remain uncertain [f2377, f9800, f2865].
